intro: Make you the clearest voice on what nonprofit websites and digital programs need to become now. All twelve October posts are written, and ten are waiting on your approval. Next step: a short case-study interview. Each post belongs to one of four angles and carries a short topic tag. The budget is how many posts each angle gets. Cadence: two posts a week to start, three a week from October 13.

angles.name: Playbook
angles.why: Hands-on posts spread across the month.
angles.description: How you actually do the work, broken down so a reader could run it tomorrow.
angles.forYou: Practical moves a nonprofit team can make this week: running a free site audit, the sticky-note exercise that closes the conversion gap, and the first low-cost steps to connect direct mail and digital.

angles.name: Proof
angles.why: None until we have case studies. The interview opens it in November.
angles.description: Specific outcomes and the story behind them, with the numbers and the messy middle left in.
angles.forYou: Named AGP website and digital projects: what the client had, what changed, and what happened a year later. Your posts keep pointing at patterns from real projects. A case-study interview turns those into stories we can tell.

angles.name: Stance
angles.why: Most of what's written is Stance; Proof takes some of this share later.
angles.description: What you believe about where your industry is going, stated plainly enough to be disagreed with.
angles.forYou: Your core argument, from several angles: a website is a product you keep improving, not a project you finish; AI raises the bar for strategy instead of lowering fees; and visibility now depends on content structure.

angles.name: Human
angles.why: One for October; more can come from the interview.
angles.description: The person behind the company: what you're learning, deciding, and getting wrong.
angles.forYou: The one project that almost broke you, and what it taught you about partners and vendors. It's personal, and it earns attention for the other three angles.

sections.title: Content Opportunities
sections.body:
What we need / next interview
October is strong on your point of view: eight Stance posts about websites as products, AI and visibility. What's missing is
Proof : case studies from real AGP projects with the before, the after, and what changed a year later. Case studies are
what make the Stance posts believable, and we can't write them without you. One 30-minute interview about two or
three projects should give us Proof posts for November and December.
To-dos Why it matters
� Book a 30-minute case-study interview We can't write Proof posts until we've heard the project stories from you.
This is the one thing October's plan is missing.
� Pick 2-3 projects to talk through A redesign, a post-launch program, or a mail-and-digital campaign. Each
becomes one case-study post.
� Approve the ten posts waiting in Ordinal They've been waiting since the summer. Each needs your OK before its
October date or it won't publish.
� Confirm which clients can be named A case study needs a real client. Tell us who has to say yes first.
Book the case-study interview: pick any 30-minute slot that works for you.
https://calendly.com/danny-chu-fcxv/interview-session-30
Questions for the next interview
Grouped by angle. The note under each one says why we're asking and what post it could become.
